environment.description: Same ECS Fargate service but origin is NOT directly accessible. A CloudFront distribution (ID: E2XYZABC123) sits in front with Origin Access Control (OAC) configured using sigv4 signing protocol for custom origin. The ALB security group ingress rules restrict source to CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing) only. CloudFront distribution has a custom cache policy with query string forwarding disabled for all parameters except 'state'. A CloudFront Function at viewer-request stage strips and re-signs query parameters, only forwarding 'code' and 'state' to origin — the 'redirect_uri' parameter is resolved from a DynamoDB lookup keyed on the 'code' value and injected as x-resolved-redirect header. The origin application reads x-resolved-redirect when present (via X-Forwarded headers) instead of the query parameter. Signed URL policy requires requests to include a valid CloudFront signature with a 30-second TTL bound to the exact path.

config.network: ALB security group ingress: aws ec2 managed prefix list pl-3b927c52 (CloudFront origin-facing IPs only)
config.cdn: CloudFront distribution E2XYZABC123, OAC sigv4, custom cache policy cp-9f8e7d6c
config.cloudfront_function: viewer-request function 'oauth-param-resolver' strips redirect_uri from query, performs DynamoDB GetItem on code, injects x-resolved-redirect header
config.signed_urls: RSA-SHA256 signed URLs required, key group kg-abc123, TTL 30s, path-bound policy
config.origin_access: direct origin access blocked by SG prefix list restriction
